cards.title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber; Gemini 4 Pre-Training Underway
cards.why_it_matters: Major flagship releases from Google DeepMind that the whole field will benchmark against, with concrete efficiency and coding gains relevant to anyone building agentic systems.
cards.summary: Gemini 3.6 Flash improves over 3.5 Flash with 17% fewer output tokens (Artificial Analysis Index), DeepSWE score 49% vs. 37%, MLE Bench 63.9% vs. 49.7%, and OSWorld-Verified 83.0% vs. 78.4%, priced at $1.50/$7.50 per 1M input/output tokens. 3.5 Flash-Lite hits 350 output tokens/second. A new cyber-specialized 3.5 Flash Cyber model pairs with the CodeMender agent. Gemini 4 pre-training has begun.

cards.title: NVIDIA Cosmos-H-Dreams: Real-Time Generative Simulator for Surgical Robotics
cards.why_it_matters: Bridges world models and interactive RL environments — a concrete example of distilling a large video world model into a real-time causal student for closed-loop policy evaluation without physical hardware.
cards.summary: Cosmos-H-Dreams distills NVIDIA's Cosmos-H-Surgical-Simulator (built on Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B) into a causal, few-step student model served via FlashDreams on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU. It takes an RGB frame plus live robot kinematics and autoregressively generates future surgical video, enabling real-time closed-loop policy evaluation. Trained on dVRK tabletop suturing including failure episodes; also demonstrated on the Versius surgical platform.

cards.title: Negative Branch Asymmetry in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation Under CFG: Diagnosis and Fix via Positive-Direction Matching
cards.why_it_matters: Identifies and resolves a concrete failure mode in CFG-guided on-policy distillation — directly relevant to anyone working on diffusion distillation or video generation fine-tuning pipelines.
cards.summary: On-policy distillation that naively matches CFG-composed teacher/student velocities is under-identified: positive- and negative-branch errors can trade off. When the teacher's negative branch holds privileged information unavailable to the student, this causes Negative Branch Asymmetry (NBA), increasing negative-branch error while reducing positive-branch error. The proposed Positive-Direction Matching (PDM) separately constrains the positive prediction and CFG conditional direction, yielding more robust distillation in dense-to-sparse video control experiments.

cards.title: ClinFusion: Medical MLLM with Cascaded 2D/3D Vision Encoder Beats GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3-Flash on Most Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a novel cascaded encoder architecture unifying 2D and native 3D medical imaging, relevant to anyone working on multimodal architectures or medical AI evals.
cards.summary: ClinFusion introduces a cascaded Spatial-Aware Locality Fusion encoder unifying 2D and 3D medical image understanding. It achieves SOTA on 20 of 24 benchmarks vs. open-source medical MLLMs and outperforms GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3-Flash on 13 of 16 multimodal benchmarks. New eval tools include MedIF-Bench and an ROI-grounded report evaluation metric validated by board-certified radiologists.

cards.title: TemporalSinkhorn: Parallel-in-Time Entropic Optimal Transport with Certified Accuracy for Flow Matching
cards.why_it_matters: Directly accelerates the entropic OT solves inside Flow Matching training pipelines with provable correctness guarantees — a niche but practically useful result for researchers training flow-based generative models.
cards.summary: TemporalSinkhorn parallelizes Sinkhorn iterations across time using a certified safe-prefix mechanism that guarantees output accuracy is never speculative. On 4 A100s with n=2048, it achieves 1.42x–3.55x wall-time speedup over sequential warm-start across synthetic streams and 3.054x–3.632x on Flow Matching minibatch streams, with zero marginal-tolerance violations. A separate RTX 4060 test yields 4.315x geometric-mean speedup.

cards.title: PAC Learning from Conditional Samples Across Heterogeneous Data Providers: Sample Complexity Ranges from Linear to Quadratic
cards.why_it_matters: Provides theoretical grounding for when distributed or federated learning from restricted conditional queries is sample-efficient — relevant background for anyone designing multi-provider data pipelines or studying learning theory.
cards.summary: Studies distribution learning where queries return conditional samples from sets in a fixed family. Learnability depends on the co-occurrence graph: PAC learning requires a complete co-occurrence graph, with worst-case complexity Õ(n²/ε²). A hierarchical comparability condition on the query family yields near-linear Õ(n/ε²) complexity. Every polynomial rate between linear and quadratic is achievable for some query family.
